$comment: Pinned, SHA-verified HarfBuzz SOURCE release tarball for the M7 runtime-UI text shaper (src/packages/ui/text/, issue #237 / R-UI-005; a8 text-shaping). SINGLE source of truth for the pin — read by cmake/ContextHarfBuzz.cmake (string(JSON)) which fetches + verifies (cmake/ContextDownload.cmake) + extracts + builds the AMALGAMATED single translation unit src/harfbuzz.cc into the `harfbuzz` static target (DECISION-a7a8-deps.md: 'HarfBuzz: use the amalgamated single-TU src/harfbuzz.cc'). Like FreeType (and unlike the MSVC/Clang-ABI prebuilts V8/wgpu-native/CEF/wasmtime), HarfBuzz is portable C++ built FROM SOURCE here, so it compiles under the local Strawberry-GCC dev gate AND all three CI build legs (and the Emscripten web target) with no prebuilt and no toggle. The amalgamated TU pulls only HarfBuzz's built-in OpenType shaper + its bundled Unicode Character Database (hb-ucd.cc) — NO external Unicode/ICU/glib/FreeType provider is enabled (no HAVE_* defines), so no transitive dependency enters the shipped engine and the FreeType<->HarfBuzz circular option stays severed (FreeType built with FT_DISABLE_HARFBUZZ; R-SEC-006). The official meson-dist release tarball is byte-stable (an uploaded release asset, not a regenerated git-archive); the pin below is that artifact's SHA-256. Upstream COPYING is vendored verbatim under third_party/harfbuzz/ (NOTICE flow-down); tools/license-allowlist.json records 'harfbuzz':'MIT-Modern-Variant' ('Old MIT' — added to allowed_licenses).
$comment_mirrors: AVAILABILITY (issue #359): HarfBuzz shares FreeType's blast radius — the SAME package (src/packages/ui/text/) fetches both at CONFIGURE time in the DEFAULT build, so one host being down reds the whole rollup. The #359 sweep found GitHub Releases is materially more reliable than savannah's dispatcher (and correlated with CI itself — a GitHub outage stops the checkout anyway), but single-sourced is still single-sourced, so a verified fallback is listed. `url` (upstream home) is tried FIRST; `mirrors` only after it is exhausted, verified against the SAME `sha256` — a mirror serving different bytes is REFUSED and skipped, and the fetch still fails CLOSED when no source yields the pinned artifact (R-SEC-009). The mirror is Fedora's CONTENT-ADDRESSED lookaside cache, which stores the exact upstream tarball keyed by its SHA-512 — hence `sha512` below, whose ONLY purpose is to build that URL (the authoritative pin remains `sha256`, checked on arrival regardless of source). Verified byte-identical (18057576 bytes) on 2026-07-25. Two candidates the sweep REJECTED, recorded so they are not re-tried: www.freedesktop.org/software/harfbuzz/release/ (404 — that path is retired) and the Debian pool (404 — carries a different version). On a VERSION BUMP the mirror URL needs BOTH the new version AND the new tarball's SHA-512 re-embedded; tools/check_source_pins.py enforces version coherence and that the URL's embedded /sha512/<hex>/ equals the declared `sha512`, so a half-updated mirror fails python-tests instead of quietly pointing at the wrong tarball. That gate is OFFLINE and STRUCTURAL — a well-formed lookaside URL that Fedora has since rotated out still passes it — so re-fetching the candidate and re-comparing its SHA-256 on every bump remains the author's duty. Note this pin has ONE mirror, and Fedora's lookaside only carries versions Fedora packages: a future bump may need a different fallback rather than a re-pointed one.
